transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I hope I’m not wasting anyone’s time, but I’ve been having a situation at my apartment building for a few months now. It’s gotten… difficult to ignore.

The property manager, and a few people in the building, seem to be using things like mail being “accidentally” delivered wrong, noises in the walls at certain times, and little comments from neighbors to sort of pressure me to leave. They have explanations and paperwork, of course, but the pattern is still there. I thought it would be best to talk to someone about it, just to make sure I’m handling it appropriately.
Do you think the property manager and neighbors are actually trying to harass you?

I mean… yes, I do think that’s what’s happening. I don’t want to sound unreasonable, and I know they can point to paperwork or say it’s all just mistakes, but over the past few months the same things keep happening—my mail ending up wrong, noises in the walls at particular times, neighbors making these little comments.

Taken one by one, maybe it sounds like nothing. But the pattern feels pretty clear to me, like they’re trying to push me out of the apartment. I’m saying that carefully, doctor, because I know how it can sound, but I don’t think I’m imagining the pattern.
Have you ever felt like you were being harassed or targeted like this before?

Not like this, no. I mean, I don’t want to make it sound dramatic or like I’m accusing everyone of something, but this has been going on for months now at my apartment.

It’s the property manager and certain people in the building—mail being misdelivered, noises in the walls at certain times, little comments from neighbors. They always have explanations or paperwork, and I understand that, but the pattern is still there. That’s really why I came in, to see if I’m handling it the right way.
Have you felt like you're being targeted or harassed at work or by people outside of your apartment building?

Not really at work, no… or outside the building, I wouldn’t say that. I don’t want to overstate it.

It’s mainly the apartment situation that’s been concerning me—the property manager and some people in the building. The misdelivered mail, the noises in the walls at certain times, the little comments from neighbors… they can explain each thing, and they have paperwork, I understand that. But the pattern has been going on for months, and it still feels like they’re trying to pressure me out.

I’m trying to be fair about it, doctor. I just don’t want to ignore something that seems that consistent.
Do you think anyone else in your life, outside of your apartment building, is also trying to harass you?

No, I don’t think so… not outside the building. I’m trying not to make it bigger than it is.

What I’m here about is really the apartment situation—the property manager and certain people in the building. For months it’s been the misdelivered mail, the noises in the walls at certain times, and little comments from neighbors. They always have explanations, or paperwork, and I understand that may sound reasonable to other people… but the pattern is still there to me. It feels like pressure to get me out of the apartment.
Do you think the situation at your apartment is connected to other parts of your life?

I don’t think so… not in a broad way, anyway. I’m trying to be careful not to connect things that don’t belong together.

It really seems centered on the apartment. For months, it’s been the property manager and certain people in the building—mail going to the wrong place, noises in the walls at particular times, little comments from neighbors. They’ll explain each thing, and there’s always paperwork or some reason, I understand that. But when I look at all of it together, the pattern is still there to me.

So… connected to other parts of my life? Not really. It feels more like it’s aimed at getting me out of the apartment. Does that make sense?
Do you think the people at your apartment building are the only ones trying to harass you?

As far as I can tell, yes… I mean, I don’t want to sound like I’m accusing everyone. It’s really just the property manager and certain people in the building.

For months now it’s been things like my mail ending up in the wrong place, noises in the walls at particular times, and these little comments from neighbors. They always have explanations, and I know they have paperwork for things, so maybe to someone else it sounds ordinary. But the pattern is what I can’t get past. It feels like they’re trying to pressure me out of the apartment.

I’m not saying people outside the building are involved. I’m trying to keep it to what I’ve actually noticed.
Do you think the people at your apartment building want to harm you or just make you leave?

I don’t think they want to physically harm me, no… I don’t want to say something stronger than I mean.

It feels more like they’re trying to make me leave. For months now, with the mail ending up in the wrong place, the noises in the walls at certain times, and those little comments from neighbors… it just adds up. They’ll show paperwork or give explanations, and I understand that probably sounds reasonable. But it doesn’t change the pattern I’m seeing.

So, to answer you plainly, I think it’s more pressure to get me out of the apartment than trying to hurt me. Is that… is that a fair way to put it?
Do you think you would notice if someone outside of your apartment building was trying to harass you?

I think I would notice, yes… at least I hope I would. I try to be pretty careful about not assuming things.

What I’ve actually noticed is still really centered in the building—the property manager, some neighbors, the mail being misplaced, the noises in the walls at certain times, those comments. They always have explanations and paperwork, and I’m not trying to dismiss that, but the pattern is hard for me to ignore.

Outside the apartment building, I haven’t really seen that same kind of pattern. So if someone else were doing it, I think I’d need to see something specific before I said that. Does that sound reasonable?
Do you feel like people in general are out to get you?

No, I wouldn’t say people in general are out to get me. I know that would sound… too broad, and I’m not trying to make it bigger than it is.

It’s really about the apartment building. I’m here because for months I’ve felt the property manager and certain people there have been doing these things—the mail going to the wrong place, noises in the walls at particular times, little comments from neighbors—and it feels like pressure to get me out.

They have explanations, paperwork, all of that, and I understand how it may look from the outside. But the pattern is what I keep seeing. I’m not saying everyone is against me. Just… this situation at the building. Does that make sense?
Do you think the harassment is limited to just the property manager and a few neighbors, or do you think more people might be involved?

I think… I’d put it as the property manager and certain people in the building. A few neighbors, yes. I don’t want to make it sound like some huge thing if I can’t prove that.

But it has felt coordinated in a way, with the mail being misdelivered, the noises in the walls happening at certain times, and then those little comments from people. So I can’t honestly say it’s only one person. It feels like more than just the manager.

I’m not saying everyone in the building is involved. Just that, from the pattern I keep seeing, it seems like the manager and some people there are trying to pressure me out. Even when they show paperwork or give explanations, that doesn’t really change what I’m seeing. Is that clear enough?
Have you ever had a period where you didn't feel like you were being harassed at your apartment building?

Not really, no… at least not for any meaningful stretch of time.

It started not long after I moved into the new apartment, and it’s been going on about… 11 months now. I don’t want to exaggerate it—there may be days where I try not to focus on it, or nothing obvious happens—but I can’t say there’s been a real period where I felt it had stopped.

Is that the kind of timeline you mean?
Do you think the harassment at your apartment building will ever stop?

I’d like to think it could stop, yes. I don’t want to sound hopeless about it.

But honestly… as long as the property manager and those few people in the building keep doing these things—the mail ending up wrong, the noises in the walls at certain times, the little comments from neighbors—I don’t see why it would stop on its own.

They always have explanations or paperwork, and I understand that probably sounds reasonable to other people. But the pattern is still there to me. So unless that changes, I don’t really feel like it’s going to stop. Is that… an okay way to answer?
Do you think this situation at your apartment building is an isolated incident in your life?

I guess I’d say… mostly yes, it feels centered on the apartment building. I don’t want to make it sound bigger than it is.

It’s really been the property manager and certain people there—the mail being misdelivered, the noises in the walls at particular times, and those little comments from neighbors. That’s the situation that brought me here.

I’m not saying my whole life is like that, or that everyone everywhere is involved. It’s this building, this pattern there. And I know they have paperwork and explanations, but those don’t really change what I’m seeing. Does that answer what you mean by isolated?
Do you think you would feel safe and not harassed if you were to move to a different apartment?

I think… yes, probably. If I were in a different apartment, away from that property manager and those particular people, I’d like to believe I’d feel safe.

I don’t mean to make it sound dramatic, but I’m here because for months it’s felt like they’ve been using things like the mail being misdelivered, noises in the walls at certain times, and little comments from neighbors to sort of pressure me out. And I know they have explanations and paperwork for it, but the pattern is hard for me to ignore.

So if I moved somewhere else and those things weren’t happening, I think I’d feel much better. Does that make sense?
Do you think the people harassing you at your apartment building have a personal reason for doing so?

I don’t know if I’d say it’s personal in the way of, you know, some big vendetta against me. I don’t want to overstate it.

But it does feel directed at me. For months now, the property manager and certain people in the building have been doing these things—the mail ending up wrong, noises in the walls at particular times, little comments from neighbors—and it feels like the purpose is to pressure me out of the apartment.

They always have explanations, and paperwork, and I know that probably sounds reasonable. But it doesn’t change the pattern I can see. So… personal reason? I’m not sure exactly what reason, but it feels intentional toward me. Is that answering it properly?
Do you think the people at your apartment building are harassing you for a specific reason?

I think the reason is they want me out of the apartment. I don’t know if they’d ever say it that plainly, and I’m not trying to accuse everyone of everything, but that’s what it feels like.

For months now it’s been the same sort of things—the mail going to the wrong place, noises in the walls at certain times, little comments from neighbors—and it adds up. They have paperwork and explanations, I understand that, but it doesn’t really change the pattern I’m seeing.

So yes… I think there is a specific reason, which is to pressure me to leave. Is that clear enough?
Do you feel like you're being harassed in other areas of your life besides your apartment building?

Not really, no. I mean… I don’t want to make it sound bigger than it is. It’s mostly tied to the apartment building.

What brought me here is that for months now I’ve felt like the property manager and certain people there have been using things like the mail being misdelivered, noises in the walls at certain times, and little comments from neighbors to pressure me out. They do have explanations and paperwork, I understand that, but the pattern is still there to me.

Outside of that setting, I don’t think I’m generally being harassed. It’s really the apartment situation that’s been bothering me. Does that answer what you’re asking?
Do you think others would notice the same pattern of harassment if they were in your place?

I think… yes, if they were really in my place and paying attention over time, they’d notice it too. Maybe not from one incident by itself, because any one thing can be explained away—the mail, or a noise, or a neighbor’s comment.

But after months of it, the timing and the way it all fits together… I think another person would start to see the same pattern. I know they have their paperwork and explanations, and I’m not trying to sound unreasonable, but that doesn’t change what I’m seeing.

Does that make sense?
Do you think it's possible that you're misinterpreting the actions of the property manager and neighbors?

I suppose it’s possible in the general sense… I mean, I don’t want to sit here and say I’m incapable of being wrong. I understand that people can have paperwork or explanations for things.

But honestly, Doctor, after months of this—the mail being misdelivered, the noises in the walls happening at certain times, and those little comments from neighbors—it feels like more than a misunderstanding to me. It feels coordinated, like the property manager and certain people in the building are trying to pressure me out of the apartment.

I’m trying to be fair about it, I really am. But the pattern is still there, even if they explain each individual thing. Does that sound… I mean, is that answering your question?
